story_type: rescue swimmer helmet camera, wading through floodwater to a basket hoist
hook: She was about to ride a rescue basket out of the floodwater.
narration: She was about to ride a rescue basket out of Hurricane Florence's floodwater.
This is North Carolina, September nineteenth, twenty eighteen, seen from a Coast Guard rescue swimmer's helmet.
He pushed through submerged barbed wire fences, floating fire ant beds and chest deep water.
He found two people still standing in the flood.
He led them back through the water, one step at a time.
A rescue basket is the safest ride for someone with no training. You just sit inside and hold on.
[short pause] Then he signaled the helicopter overhead to lift.
outcome: And the basket carried her up, out of the floodwater.
title: Rescue swimmer's helmet cam in a flood
description:
After Hurricane Florence on Sept. 19, 2018, a Coast Guard rescue swimmer from Air Station Atlantic City worked through chest-deep floodwater in North Carolina to reach people in flooded homes, filmed on his helmet camera.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Chief Petty Officer Brad Fitzpatrick, Air Station Atlantic City, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/627892/coast-guard-air-station-atlantic-city-rescues-people-and-pets-during-hurricane-florence-response
